decisions.summary: Supplier master must include the legal, tax, purchasing, receiving and payee setup required by downstream purchase-to-pay workflows; transaction records remain owned by Procurement, Inventory and Finance.
The same user profiles that can access Suppliers may view tax and bank fields; changes remain auditable and use supplier-management actions.
Broad tax/bank visibility conflicts with the ERP core access model and must be reconciled before design is approved for planning.
CSV catalog import remains optional and reviewed; manual entry is the baseline.

actions: Reconciled the user-expanded P2P Supplier master scope across discovery, ledger, README, expected-versus-existing matrix and platform evidence.
Updated the benchmark to five official sources covering supplier setup, offers, bank-account controls, orders and receipts; separated industry baseline from LoopDev decisions.
Recorded supplier legal/tax identity, contacts/addresses, purchase defaults, Finance references, payee instructions and SupplierItem purchasing terms.
Kept purchase orders, actual receipts, supplier invoices and payment execution as separate downstream transactions; no production code or implementation tasks were added.
Revalidated the completed discovery handoff after design clarified shared capability semantics; no product scope changed.

requirements.evidence: ERP ownership, identity, same Product-access role population and P2P master direction are documented; lifecycle, field policy and authorization mapping remain design decisions.
P2P master field inventory and broad field visibility are recorded; jurisdiction rules, access-model reconciliation, verification and audit behavior need design.
SupplierItem cardinality and purchasing terms are documented; Product-versus-variant mapping and CSV contract remain open.
Downstream transaction boundaries are defined; Procurement, Inventory and Finance contracts are not in this module scope.
